foreign.specTerm: Facet, or Interceptor for a hook

reviewed.reason: ActorActivation is the live half of the §8.1 Actor lifecycle (recover state before serving); the SPEC names the lifecycle obligations but no noun for the in-memory instance.
TenantBootstrapAnchor is the first trust record a Tenant boots from; §3.3 describes the recorded trust configuration without naming the boot record.
TurnPromptAssembler is the agentive form of the SPEC's own prompt.assemble cut point (§4.4, §5.6); the SPEC names the act, not the actor.
ValidationAttestation records that a required validator actually ran; implementation evidence machinery beneath the SPEC's altitude.
Agentive form of the authenticate step in the §8.5 dispatcher order; the SPEC names the act, not the actor.
CommitCertainty classifies how much is durably known about a failed §8.5 command's commit (notAttempted, rolledBack, unknown); the SPEC prescribes the retry behavior but names no axis.
OperationPayloadCardinality and MediatedReplayCardinality name the SPEC §7.3 single-versus-nonempty-batch payload discriminator precisely while the versioned wire field remains shape.
CompatRange is the exact public type used by the §4.1 FacetManifest interface; the canonical prose model excludes its fenced TypeScript declaration.
ActorCloneOwnedState carries owned records for the §8.5 Workspace-portability command family; the SPEC names the family, not the copied payload.
ConfirmedOperationFailure is a failure carrying durable evidence, the opposite of §7.4's indeterminate; §7.4's word 'final' names Receipt lineage, not an error class.
PackageDependency names §9.1 'code references' between Packages with the ecosystem's word; the SPEC deliberately keeps the package shape's internals open.
DesiredProjection is reconciliation vocabulary (desired versus observed) for §9.3 idempotent materialization; the SPEC describes reconciling without the adjective.
InvocationPublicationDrainer drains the post-commit publication outbox behind §7.4 delivery; agentive implementation noun.
PackageCodeEntrypoint names the module a §9.1 code reference loads first, following the ecosystem's word; the SPEC keeps package code shape open.
PackageModuleEvaluator executes §9.1 package code; the SPEC says Packages are inspectable without execution but names no executing component.
AuthorityPermitExpectation is the consuming Actor's precomputed view of a §10.3 cross-Actor permit; an implementation record the SPEC does not name.
ProtocolIdFactory is the id-construction seam substrates supply to the §8.5 dispatcher; a generic construction-role noun beneath the SPEC's altitude.
RunGenesis and TurnGenesis are the creation records the §5.2 runtime consumes; the SPEC describes creation without naming the record handed in.
The Init suffix names constructor-argument records throughout the codebase; a code-organization convention beneath the SPEC's altitude.
PackageModuleInspector reads §9.1 package code without executing it; the SPEC requires inspectability but names no inspecting component.
InterceptContext and InterceptResult implement the abstract intercept method declared by the §4.4 fenced interface; visible prose uses the related Interceptor noun.
PackageLock pins a resolved §9.1 dependency closure, following the ecosystem's lockfile idiom.
MediaHint classifies ContentStore payload metadata below the §8.2 content-custody contract; the SPEC does not name this optional implementation hint.
MetadataSnapshot is the versioned release listing a §9.1 package registry serves; registry vocabulary the SPEC leaves to registry governance.
The Options suffix names optional constructor configuration records; a code-organization convention beneath the SPEC's altitude.
ActorPlan and MaterializationPlan stage §9.3 reconciliation into an inspectable step list before application; the SPEC prescribes idempotent materialization, not its intermediate.
MediatedInvocationPreflight is the §7.3 pre-interceptor replay-record lookup ('before any mutating interceptor runs, the host atomically looks up'); the SPEC mandates the step without naming it.
ProtocolCommandRegistration records one command family with the §8.5 dispatcher; the SPEC names registries, not the act of joining one.
MaterializationRollout orders §9.3 reconciliation on a live platform so existing RunPins stay resolvable; deployment vocabulary the SPEC does not use.
SemVer is the exact version type used throughout the SPEC's fenced interfaces; the export-name tokenizer exposes its Sem and Ver fragments separately.
TransientContent* hold content no durable record owns yet, bridging put and first retained owner under §8.2 custody; the SPEC describes ownership, not the interim state.
UnpreparedPayload is the payload before §7.3 preparation freezes it; the negation of the SPEC's own word.
TurnModelUsage reports model token accounting through the §5.6 executor seam; provider-API vocabulary with no SPEC counterpart.
